title: The verifier slices at every cut Z: an interpolated ramp turns 3 planes into 1,700 and minutes into hours

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent

body:
The verifier slices the part at every distinct cut Z. A path with an interpolated ramp has about 1,700 cut planes instead of the 3 cut levels, and the band-reach and tangency laws then take minutes. The same path takes 89.6 s as a whole suite on main.

## Evidence

From PR #3577's head (one Waterline Outside generation, debug, temporary counters, reverted):

- The generator is fast: `ring_plan_ramped` 110 ms; each level walk 1.5 to 1.8 ms; 186 `dead_end_ramp`/`push_zig` calls are all in microseconds.
- The path is 8,850 moves and 8,553 feed moves, with 1,697 distinct feed-move Z values (the cut levels are 3: z = 12, 2, 1.5).
- The time is in the verify laws:
  - `section::tangency` 28.3 s;
  - `section::solid` 0.82 s;
  - `band_reach` plane sections and grid 1.4 s, with 5,596,906 boundary samples at a 2.75 mm cell;
  - `band_reach` verdict loop: moves 0 to 6000 in 55 ms (all skipped by the `h0 >= stock_top_z` guard), then more than 148 s without finishing for the remaining 2,850 moves; single moves take 2.8 s and 28 s, about 150k `sample_tests` per move.

The unmodified single test was killed at 120 s: 100 percent CPU, 0.1 s system time, 471 MB RSS. It is CPU-bound.

## Cause

The new dead-end entry posts a zig-zag ramp, one feed move per thinned vertex per lap (`crates/motion/src/links.rs`, `push_zig`). `Rest::new` (`crates/sim/src/verify/rest.rs:89-100`) records one cut per feed chord, keyed on `m.to.z`. The path therefore has about 1,700 distinct cut planes. `band_reach_counted` (`crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs:47`, the plane loop at 102-110 and the verdict loop near 205-240) slices the part at every distinct cut Z, so the work is `O(feed_moves x samples)`, and samples grow with the plane count: quadratic in the number of ramp Z steps. `section::tangency` (`crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:89-146`) pays the same per-distinct-Z cost through `rest.islands_at`.

The new planner code is ruled out: `level_order.rs`, `level_rings.rs` (`order`, `unswept`, `too_short_at`), `level_ramp_entry.rs`, `descent.rs::ramp_fallback`, `links.rs::plan_zig_capped/push_zig` and the `arc_cross` retries are all sub-millisecond to about 100 ms.

## Recommended fix

In `band_reach_counted`, build the sampled plane set from the cut LEVELS (feed moves with `|from.z - to.z| < z_tol`) plus the deepest cut, instead of every `rest.cut()` record, and pass that set to the same `islands_at` and `boundary_samples` code. For this path that is 3 to 4 planes and restores the pre-PR cost; the same plane set also removes the 28 s in `section::tangency`.

This slightly reduces wall-sample coverage for ramps between levels. The heavy lanes on a sloped or stepped fixture must show that the verdicts do not change before it merges. A lower-risk variant is to quantize the plane key and cap the sample count.

## Why #3595 did not cover it

#3595 (`9a7de3781`) made the sample lookup exact and fast. It did not reduce the number of planes, so the per-plane cost stays.

## Related

- #3577: the ramp entry that exposes this; blocked until this is fixed.
- #3588: the verifier speed work, closed by #3595.
- #3587: the slow pin as a test-speed item.
